glossaryTerms.definition: A Greek custard pie made with semolina cream filling baked inside filo pastry and soaked in lemon syrup.

content.text: This galaktoboureko serves 8 and requires 40 minutes of preparation plus 50 minutes of baking. A thick, set custard filling sits inside crisp pastry, then the whole pie is soaked in lemon-scented syrup as soon as it comes out of the oven.

The syrup must go onto the pie while the pie is hot and the syrup is cold, or vice versa. Hot syrup on a hot pie results in a soggy pastry. Make the syrup ahead of time and refrigerate it so it is ready the moment the tin comes out of the oven.

items.prepNote: used in place of semolina to thicken the custard

content.text: Make the syrup first so it can cool. Combine the syrup sugar, honey, lemon juice and 150ml water in the medium saucepan. Bring to the boil, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then simmer for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, add the rose water if using, and refrigerate until cold.

Heat the oven to 180C. Make the custard. Whisk the eggs, custard sugar and plain flour together in a bowl until smooth. Heat the milk in the cleaned saucepan until just below the boil. Pour the hot milk slowly into the egg mixture, whisking constantly, then return the whole mixture to the pan.

Cook the custard over a medium heat, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or whisk, for 8 to 10 minutes until very thick. It should hold a trail on the surface. Remove from the heat and stir in the 40g butter and lemon zest. Cover the surface with a circle of baking paper to stop a skin forming.

Grease the rectangular baking tin with melted butter. Layer half the filo sheets in the tin, brushing each generously with melted butter and letting the edges overhang. Pour in the warm custard and spread evenly.
Fold the overhanging pastry up over the custard. Layer the remaining filo sheets on top, brushing each with butter. Tuck the edges down the sides of the tin. Score the top lightly into portions.

Bake for 45 to 50 minutes until the pastry is deep golden and the filling is fully set. Remove from the oven and immediately pour the cold syrup slowly and evenly over the hot pie. Let the syrup soak in for at least 30 minutes before cutting and serving.

items.solution: The milk was added too quickly or the heat was too high. Add the hot milk very slowly to the egg mixture while whisking, then cook on medium heat only.

items.problem: The pastry is soggy after adding the syrup
items.solution: Both the pie and the syrup must not be the same temperature. The syrup must be cold when it goes onto the hot pie, or the pie cold when the syrup is hot.

items.problem: The custard filling has not set properly
items.solution: The plain flour needs adequate cooking time in the custard to activate fully. Stir and cook until genuinely thick before filling the pie.

content.text: is one of the grand celebration desserts of Greek patisserie. It appears at Easter, at name-day gatherings and at the sort of long family lunches that stretch well into the afternoon. The syrup soak is not optional; it is what transforms a baked custard pie into something distinctly Greek in character. It keeps at room temperature for a day, covered, and can be refrigerated for up to three days.
